# Software is communication

## The package is the message

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The paper is read once. The package runs on data we never see, for
  analysts we never meet
- Users run the defaults, so the defaults are the advice
- All of them are used by public health departments, including CDC,
  UKHSA, RKI, ECDC and WHO
- In some cases the package is too complex for anyone else to use
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
| Package | Since | Stars | CRAN |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `EpiNow2` | 2020 | 141 | 58,073 |
| `epinowcast` | 2021 | 67 | not on CRAN |
| `epidist` | 2023 | 16 | not on CRAN |
| `primarycensored` | 2024 | 9 | 11,294 |
| `baselinenowcast` | 2025 | 10 | 1,678 |

::: {.attribution}
Table and the last two bullets from the
[JuliaCon 2026 roadmap deck](https://samabbott.co.uk/JuliaCon2026/roadmap/slides.html),
August 2026. Stars from the GitHub API, downloads CRAN totals from
[cranlogs](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/), both to mid August 2026
:::
:::
::::

## Defaults are advice

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- [EpiNow2](https://epiforecasts.io/EpiNow2/) has been on CRAN since
  1 September 2020
- CDC used it for nowcasts and $R_t$ until June 2026
- Every argument a user leaves alone is a decision they inherited from
  us. The generation time, the delays, the prior on $R_t$, the sampler
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
```r
estimates <- epinow(
  data = reported_cases,
  generation_time = gt_opts(example_generation_time),
  delays = delay_opts(example_incubation_period + reporting_delay),
  rt = rt_opts(prior = LogNormal(mean = 2, sd = 0.2)),
  stan = stan_opts(cores = 4)
)
```

::: {.attribution}
[EpiNow2 vignette](https://epiforecasts.io/EpiNow2/articles/EpiNow2.html) ·
[CRAN archive](https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/EpiNow2/),
1.1.0 on 1 September 2020 ·
[CDC CFA, Behind the model: nowcasting](https://www.cdc.gov/cfa-behind-the-model/php/data-research/nowcasting.html),
January 2026, and the CFA $R_t$ page's switch of method for dates after
1 June 2026
:::
:::
::::

## Limitations first

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The live Bundibugyo report puts its limitations before the methods,
  in bullets, most consequential first
- The feedback we got is that this is off-putting
- The dashboard hid its limits on a page few reached. This report leads
  with them and people stop reading
- How should we warn?

> Every estimate is a model-based extrapolation under strong assumptions,
> not a measurement.
>
> *Abbott, Sherratt, Brand and Funk, 2026*
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}

## Evaluation as communication

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A forecast hub is an agreement. Same targets, same dates, same
  quantiles, same score
- Agreeing how to score is agreeing what a good forecast is. WIS is the
  hubs' headline measure
- [scoringutils](https://epiforecasts.io/scoringutils/) implements the
  scores. Pairwise comparison on the overlapping forecasts gives a
  relative skill that teams who miss weeks can still read
- UKHSA, the UK Health Security Agency, asked us for guidance on
  evaluation. Practice still differs between agencies
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-pairwise-illustration.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Three models compared in pairs to give a relative skill score"}

::: {.attribution}
Figure from the
[scoringutils manuscript](https://github.com/epiforecasts/scoringutils/tree/main/inst/manuscript),
Bosse et al. · UKHSA request and the relative WIS versus MAE difference
from the `bmbr-guidance-grant` project notes
:::

## Community as the channel

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- [epinowcast](https://www.epinowcast.org/). Over 50 researchers and
  public health analysts, 31 seminars from May 2023 to May 2026
- A forum, a monthly meeting with a rotating chair, release notes that
  name everyone who reported a bug or joined a discussion
- I am also interested in why efforts in this direction keep failing

> Trying to build a community of practice as community >> methods or
> models alone.
>
> *Abbott, 2023*
:::
